extracted.intended_audience: financially under-resourced independent inventors and small businesses seeking pro bono patent assistance (and regional program administrators / volunteer practitioners)
extracted.subtask_short: applying for patent pro bono assistance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on eligibility, matching, and working with volunteer patent practitioners through the USPTO Patent Pro Bono Program, including income and documentary requirements, micro-entity rules, timelines, and practitioner engagement expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program eligibility — financially under-resourced
rubrics_metrics.description: Assists financially under-resourced independent inventors and small businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional programs generally limit eligibility to applicants with gross household income usually limited to 300% of the federal poverty guidelines (regional program dependent). Example given: a single person could have an income of up to $38,280 (see federal poverty guidelines). The income limit increases with additional dependents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated knowledge of the patent system
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must demonstrate knowledge of the patent system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical ways to demonstrate knowledge: have at least a provisional application on file with the USPTO or have completed a certificate training course (also available in Spanish). Regional programs screen for knowledge of the patent system as part of eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive subject matter — 'more than an idea'
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must have an invention (more than an idea).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To demonstrate that there is an invention one should be able to describe the invention so that someone could make and use the invention. Regional programs screen to ensure applicants have an actual invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant responsible for USPTO fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are responsible for all USPTO fees associated with filing and prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Micro-entity status provides a 75% reduction in USPTO fees (see micro-entity criteria). Regional programs may charge an application fee of $25-$150. The guidance emphasizes: 'You are responsible for USPTO fees - do not ask the practitioner to advance or pay your USPTO fees.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and deadlines for applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants with upcoming deadlines may not be able to be matched with a practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a provisional application on file, your regional program may only attempt to match you with a practitioner if you apply 3-6 months in advance of your provisional application's expiration date. This allows time to find a practitioner and time for the practitioner to complete the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional program autonomy and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional programs follow general USPTO guidelines but are independent and set their own policies and procedures; they screen and match applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional programs may cover individual or multiple states and are operated by nonprofits, universities, or bar associations. They are responsible for screening applicants (income, knowledge of patent system, actual invention) and matching applicants with volunteer practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro-entity status criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A micro entity is a patent applicant who certifies that he/she meets statutory requirements to obtain a 75% reduction in USPTO fees under the AIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AIA micro-entity requirements listed: (1) Qualifies as a small entity; (2) Has not been named as an inventor on more than 4 previously filed patent applications; (3) Did not, in the calendar year preceding the calendar year in which the applicable fee is paid, have a gross income exceeding 3 times the median household income; (4) Has not assigned, granted, or conveyed (and is not under obligation to do so) a license or other ownership interest in the application concerned to an entity that, in the calendar year preceding the calendar year in which the applicable fee is paid, had a gross income exceeding 3 times the median household income.

rubrics_metrics.name: No guarantee of practitioner match
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if you qualify for pro bono assistance, there is no guarantee that a practitioner will choose to work with you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional program provides volunteer practitioners with a brief description of you and your invention, but practitioners may decline. Reasons an invention may not be chosen include, but are not limited to: no practitioner with experience in your technology; you or your invention/business conflicts with an existing or former client of the practitioner. Follow up periodically with your regional program; if no practitioner is available, the program will inform you and may provide other resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching exclusion factors (conflict or expertise)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners may refuse matches due to lack of technical experience or conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit examples: 'No practitioner with experience in your technology' and 'You or your invention/business conflicts with an existing or former client of the practitioner.' These are listed as non-exhaustive reasons a practitioner may not choose to work with an inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant engagement expectations when matched
rubrics_metrics.description: If matched with a practitioner, the applicant must be an active participant in preparing and filing the patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be able to describe their invention, its inventive feature(s), and the problem they are trying to solve; know their marketplace and be aware of similar inventions or solutions; be responsive to the practitioner's requests. The guidance emphasizes avoiding verbal agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement letter / retainer agreement contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may require you to sign an engagement letter or retainer agreement that documents the representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such letters may discuss information including, but not limited to: the scope of services provided; any ancillary fees; the reasons that the practitioner may withdraw from the representation. The practitioner must obtain your informed consent to limit the scope of services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited (unbundled) scope of services
rubrics_metrics.description: Volunteer practitioners may provide limited or 'unbundled' services covering only portions of the patenting process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent application process stages include preparation and filing of the patent application, response to USPTO communications, and payment of periodic maintenance fees if granted. Example: practitioner may help prepare and file the application but may not agree to help with other stages. The practitioner must obtain informed consent to limit the scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancillary fees (drawings and others)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to USPTO fees, applicants may need to pay ancillary fees such as drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional guidance notes that ancillary fees may apply and should be disclosed in the engagement letter/retainer. Applicants remain responsible for such fees even when representation is pro bono for legal services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program goals / benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Program aims to increase participation and filings, improve patent quality, and supplement pro se assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits listed include: increased participation in the patent system; increases patent application filings; improved patent quality; supplements pro se assistance efforts; opportunity for inventors to work with experienced patent practitioners; over $26.5M in donated legal services provided to inventors from 2015 to present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application process — where to apply and contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must apply directly with their regional program; USPTO provides a map and state selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To find the regional program that serves you, see www.uspto.gov/probonopatents for a map of the United States and select your state. Email probono@uspto.gov for questions. Regional programs may have their own application procedures and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up and alternative resources if unmatched
rubrics_metrics.description: If not matched with a practitioner, applicants should follow up and may be referred to other resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional programs may provide other resources to help pursue the patent application. USPTO resources referenced include the Pro Se Assistance Program (phone and URL), Inventors Assistance Center (formats and forms), and scam prevention resources.
